warnings: RULE-4 DECISION -- the '0.075' vs '1.20' pattern at ค/ก and at grid 1/11 are treated as TWO INDEPENDENT dimensions measured from the same grid line (parallel annotations), NOT a nested/additive chain summing to 1.275. Evidence: (a) A-03 site plan and E-02 lighting plan print ONLY '1.20' at ค/ก with no 0.075 sub-tick, yet both independently confirm the SAME @8.400/@-1.200 points that S-01/S-02/S-03/A-04/A-05/A-06(gable lower chain)/A-07(section1 lower chain) reach when their 0.075+1.20 stacked pair is read as parallel-not-summed; (b) if additive, the total would be @8.475/@-1.275, which no sheet's simpler '1.20'-only chain would independently corroborate. Reading them as additive (grid+0.075+1.20=1.275) was considered and rejected for this reason, though it is recorded as a live possibility for the roof-level barge-board chain specifically (see the dimension_chains note on that entry) since its printed total (8.475) numerically equals ค+1.275 and has no independent simpler confirmation either way.

The 0.075m ticks are included as genuine axis dummy points (@7.275/@-0.075 y-axis, @-0.075/@36.075 x-axis) rather than excluded as 'inside one element's own detail', because on every sheet they are printed IN LINE with the grid-spacing dimension chain (stacked directly with the 3.60/1.20 segments as one continuous vertical/horizontal dimension run), which spec's own rule-4 text frames as the deciding factor ('Rule 4 is about dimension rows that run along the building's grid axes') -- not their coincidental numeric equality to the B1 beam's half-depth (WF150/2=75mm). No beam or column element currently has an endpoint at these points; per rule 4 that is expected and does not disqualify them ('It doesn't matter whether any element sits on it'). Note @-0.075 appears on BOTH the x-axis (before grid1) and the y-axis (before ก) -- these are two different lines on two different axes that happen to share the same offset value; gridfix.py should not conflate them.

The gable-elevation/section1 ROOF-level chain ('1.125/6.15/1.20' and its mirror) is left UNRESOLVED (edge/edge) rather than forced onto a placeholder -- its own prior extraction explicitly states it 'does not correspond to a grid dimension', and while its total happens to numerically match ค+1.275 on one side, the other end (the 1.125 side) has no independent cross-check to confirm an anchor. A future pass with a higher-resolution image crop of A-06/A-07's roof-profile dimension line should resolve this rather than guessing here.

The existing z_levels entry {'id':'ระดับ','level_m':0.15,'source_image':'...หน้า09.png'} on THIS (main-building) master appears MISATTRIBUTED -- 0.15 is the สุขา block's floor level (ระดับพื้นอาคาร สุขา, confirmed on A-08/A-09/A-10/A-11) and หน้า09.png is a สุขา-block sheet, not a main-building one. This sweep does not remove or edit it (out of rule-4's scope, which only adds), but a human should decide whether to move it to the 00b master (where the identical entry already also exists) or relabel/remove it from this file.

Prime-ordering guidance for gridfix.py on the ค side: ค is the topmost/first-scanned y-axis line for this house (confirmed by direct image inspection of S-01/S-02/S-03/E-02, all of which draw ค at the top and ก at the bottom), so per spec's 'combined before+after sequence, scanned in reading order' rule (house #17's 1'/1''/1''' pattern), the FARTHER point (@8.400, beyond ค) should be named first in ค's prime sequence (encountered first scanning top-to-bottom) and the NEARER point (@7.275) second. This mirrors the already-established convention on the สุขา master, whose own ข'/ค' dummies were named 'per the reading-direction rule (y-axis scans top to bottom)' with ค as the first-scanned line there too. On the ก side (the LAST y-axis line) no such swap applies -- @-0.075 is the nearer point and @-1.200 the farther, matching a normal 'continuing past the last grid' case, nearest-first.

Every value in this sweep was cross-checked against at least 2 independent sheets (usually 3+) before being adopted as a resolved dummy point -- see the dimension_chains entries' source_image + note fields for the specific corroborating sheets. No new point was created from a single sheet's reading alone.

@-0.075 (x-axis)/@36.075 and @7.275/@-0.075/@8.400/@-1.200 (y-axis) are all genuinely unused by any element in this house's current extraction (every beam/column/footing in the elements[] arrays already resolves to a named line) -- kept per rule 4's explicit instruction ('every ... line -- even one nothing uses').
